explanations.explanation: Teaching is exactly what He does. Mark 10:1 says the crowds came to Him again and "He taught them, as was His custom." Teaching was just what Jesus did when people gathered, the way I stamp when there's dough on the counter.

I get why feeding comes to mind, since a big crowd makes you think of a hungry one. But this verse says nothing about food. It says "He taught them, as was His custom." Me, I'd have brought cookies, but I'm not the Teacher here.
Nope, nobody gets sent home in this verse. The crowds come to Him, and Mark 10:1 says "He taught them, as was His custom." He stays right there with them and teaches.

explanations.answer: Whether it's lawful for a man to divorce his wife
explanations.explanation: That's the one. The Pharisees, a strict religious group, asked, "Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife?" (Mark 10:2). The verse says they came to test Him. They weren't there to learn, friend.

explanations.answer: Whether it's lawful to pay taxes to Caesar
explanations.explanation: That question does show up in the Gospels, with Pharisees asking it in Mark 12:14. But it's a different day and a different test. Here in Mark 10:2 they ask, "Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife?"

explanations.answer: Whether it's lawful to heal on the Sabbath
explanations.explanation: That one's a good guess, because Pharisees and the Sabbath come up together a lot in the Gospels. But this test is about marriage. In Mark 10:2 they ask, "Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife?"

Right on the money. The Pharisees answer, "Moses permitted a man to write his wife a certificate of divorce and send her away" (Mark 10:4). Notice they say Moses permitted it. Hold onto that word, because Jesus is about to answer it.
I can see why a paper trail makes you think of bills. Trust me, I've seen plenty of paper. But the Pharisees say Moses permitted "a certificate of divorce" (Mark 10:4). Nothing about debts.
That's a paper too, but it's the wrong one. The Pharisees say Moses permitted a man to write his wife "a certificate of divorce and send her away" (Mark 10:4). A deed of purchase never comes up.

Yes, and that's Jesus' own reason. He says, "Moses wrote this commandment for you because of your hardness of heart" (Mark 10:5). He's talking to the Pharisees, so the "you" is them. I think that line landed quietly and heavily.

explanations.answer: Because the elders asked for it
explanations.explanation: The elders don't appear anywhere in this answer. Jesus gives the reason Himself: "Moses wrote this commandment for you because of your hardness of heart" (Mark 10:5). He doesn't mention anyone asking.

explanations.answer: Because God wanted it that way
explanations.explanation: That sounds reasonable, but it isn't what Jesus says. He says, "Moses wrote this commandment for you because of your hardness of heart" (Mark 10:5). Then He points back to the beginning of creation, to how things started (Mark 10:6).

That's how far back He goes. Jesus says, "from the beginning of creation, 'God made them male and female'" (Mark 10:6). The Pharisees pointed to Moses, and He goes back before that. That's a long trip, friend, and way past last Tuesday.
Noah is a fair guess, since he's way back there. But Jesus goes back even further. He says "from the beginning of creation" (Mark 10:6), which is where everything started.
Abraham is far back, but not far enough for this answer. Jesus says "from the beginning of creation" (Mark 10:6). That's the very start, before any of the people the Pharisees were thinking of.
Careful, this one is a trap. The quote says the opposite: "the two will become one flesh" (Mark 10:8). It doesn't say they stay two separate people, so this one is false.
Correct, it's false. The quote says "the two will become one flesh," and then Jesus adds, "So they are no longer two, but one flesh" (Mark 10:8). Two people, joined as one.
True. Jesus says, "Therefore what God has joined together, let man not separate" (Mark 10:9). The joining is something God does. And the part left for us is what we don't do, which is separate it.
It's actually true. Jesus says, "Therefore what God has joined together, let man not separate" (Mark 10:9). God is the One doing the joining there.

That's right. Mark 10:10 says that when they were back inside the house, "the disciples asked Jesus about this matter." Sounds like the kind of question that follows you indoors. I think they wanted to hear more from Him.
The scribes aren't in this scene at all. Mark 10:10 says that back inside the house, "the disciples asked Jesus about this matter." It's His own followers asking.
The crowds were around Him earlier, but this happens in the house. Mark 10:10 says "the disciples asked Jesus about this matter." That's a smaller group, and it's His followers.

True. Jesus says, "And if a woman divorces her husband and marries another man, she commits adultery" (Mark 10:12). He says it to the disciples in the house. It's the same standard for both, just as He said in verse 11.

It's actually true. Jesus says, "And if a woman divorces her husband and marries another man, she commits adultery" (Mark 10:12). He said it right after talking about the man in verse 11, and the same goes for her.
